# devStudio

> A self-hosted console that runs coding CLIs — Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, OpenCoder, and any other CLI already installed — as configurable agents. Concurrent sessions, a git worktree each, schedules, workflows and queues. Every agent runs the real CLI as a child process.

devStudio is free and open source under the MIT licence, published by Matt Ratcliffe. It runs either as a container
(`ghcr.io/matthewratcliffe/devstudio`) or as an installed desktop app on Windows, macOS and Linux.
State is JSON on a volume — there is no database, and no account to create.

The design constraint that explains most of the rest: nothing is reimplemented. When an agent works,
it is `claude`, `codex` or `opencoder` on a PATH, reading the same files it would read if the command had been
typed by hand. The orchestrator arranges the work and keeps the transcript; the CLI does the thinking.

## What it does

- [Agents](https://matthewratcliffe.github.io/devstudio/#inventory): a CLI, a system prompt, a model, a permission mode, and the skills and MCP servers it should have.
- [Sessions](https://matthewratcliffe.github.io/devstudio/#inventory): conversations running in parallel up to a configurable cap, each queueing its own turns, surviving a closed tab.
- [Repositories and worktrees](https://matthewratcliffe.github.io/devstudio/#isolation): a fresh git worktree cut per session, which is what makes running several agents at once safe rather than merely fast.
- [Workflows and schedules](https://matthewratcliffe.github.io/devstudio/#inventory): ordered steps sharing a run context, fired by cron expressions or plain timers at an agent or a workflow.
- [Skills](https://matthewratcliffe.github.io/devstudio/#inventory): reusable instruction files staged into the workspace, written by hand or pulled from the public skills.sh registry with every file they reference.
- [Team settings](https://matthewratcliffe.github.io/devstudio/#inventory): one git repository holding a team's agents, workflows, skills, schedules and standards, imported by every install; locally made definitions are never touched by a sync.
- [Model handover](https://matthewratcliffe.github.io/devstudio/#inventory): open a session on a strong model and hand over to a cheaper one after a set number of turns.
- [MCP, both directions](https://matthewratcliffe.github.io/devstudio/#inventory): attach servers to agents, and let agents call back into the orchestrator to read another session, steer a run or start one.

## Providers

- [Claude Code, OpenAI Codex and OpenCoder](https://matthewratcliffe.github.io/devstudio/#providers): built-in CLI providers with configurable models and executable settings.
- [Any installed CLI](https://matthewratcliffe.github.io/devstudio/#providers): described on a form — executable, argument template, output format — and it becomes an agent provider with no code change.
- [ACP agents](https://matthewratcliffe.github.io/devstudio/#providers): Agent Client Protocol over stdio, where permission answers come from the session's permission mode.
- [OpenAI-compatible endpoints](https://matthewratcliffe.github.io/devstudio/#providers): llama.cpp and similar. A bare model has no tools, so devStudio runs the loop itself.

## Running it

- [Container install](https://matthewratcliffe.github.io/devstudio/#install): one image, two volumes — one for state, one for the CLI logins. Published for amd64 and arm64.
- [Desktop app](https://matthewratcliffe.github.io/devstudio/#desktop): Windows, macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) and Linux. No container and no bind mounts; it uses the locally installed CLI tools and updates itself in the background.
- [Latest release and all downloads](https://github.com/matthewratcliffe/devstudio/releases/latest)
- [Container image on GHCR](https://github.com/matthewratcliffe/devstudio/pkgs/container/devstudio)

## Optional

- [Source and full documentation](https://github.com/matthewratcliffe/devstudio): the README covers configuration, instruction layering, team settings sync, the MCP surface and what changes when running without a container.
- [Contributing](https://matthewratcliffe.github.io/devstudio/#contribute): issues, pull requests and forks are all welcome; adding a CLI provider is a form rather than a patch.
